whatProducesZoningDepth.pipelineName: Factory 2 — Jurisdiction backfill factory, ZONED CITY LANE (steps Z1-Z11)
whatProducesZoningDepth.entryPoint: P:/doc_repo/90_runbooks/factory_onboarding_runbook.md section 1B; mechanical entry points in hauska-engine: scripts/onboard-preflight.mjs (gate), bake-property-atom-county.mjs (zoning-fact), depth-warm-<city>-batch.mjs (warm), cert-grade-and-report.mjs (cert), warden-sweep.mjs (audit). Stamp CLI is ldt-side: pnpm --filter @workspace/cad-ingest zoning-stamp -- --city=<key> [--dry-run]
whatProducesZoningDepth.inputRequired: A registry row carrying a live, probed zoning GIS FeatureServer layer (zoning_gis) plus an OPERATOR-RATIFIED setback table. Without zoning_gis the stamp CLI fails hard with 'unknown city' (proven on Smithville, runbook line 466). Without a ratified SETBACK_TABLES registration the draft table cannot serve.
perJurisdictionSteps: Z1 source recon — probe the live parcel layer, zoning field names, and domain-code mapping. Never template off another city's row.
Z2 registry row + zoning-stamp config — author Rail C layer, descriptor slug, per-district code-section map, railPerParcel.
Z3 setback table DRAFT — every scalar carries atom DID + verbatim quote; registration COMMENTED OUT behind TODO(<city>-review).
Z4 PLANNER row-verification — cross-check every scalar against independent extraction plus live corpus atom pulls; verify every DID resolves.
Z5 OPERATOR RATIFICATION — un-commenting the SETBACK_TABLES registration IS the ratification act.
Z6 stamp dry-run then apply (ldt side).
Z7 Tier-1 re-bake (ldt side, county-wide; monotonic-promote check required).
Z11 close — artifacts to _inbox, ledger POST, defect backlog update.
humanInLoopSteps: Z1 source recon — a human probes the FeatureServer and reads field/domain semantics. Runbook explicitly forbids templating off another city.

Z3/Z4 setback table draft and row-verification — 'Nothing mechanically grades the per-parcel record against the ordinance text; that is the Z4 planner row-verification step, A HUMAN ACT' (OPS-12_instrument_inventory.md, DEFECT CLASSES WITH NO INSTRUMENT).

Z5 OPERATOR RATIFICATION — a hard escalation point. The runbook names a setback/dimensional VALUE change as one of three things a planner must escalate to the operator and never decide unilaterally. THIS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE HUMANLESS RULING: it is not automatable by design, it is a deliberate human gate.
Z10 per-city warm script — the registry-driven single warm runner is NOT shipped (runbook planner correction 8); depth-warm-<city>-batch.mjs is hand-authored per city.
Warden scheduling — the periodic trigger did NOT ship; v1 is planner-run by hand (runbook planner correction 4).
Gate 2 operator R6 live QA — human eyes on the live surface (OPS-12).
whatProducesZoningDepth.humanlessRulingConflict: The operator's humanless ruling collides head-on with Z5. Z5 exists because no instrument grades the per-parcel setback record against ordinance text. Making L5 humanless requires EITHER building that missing instrument (an ordinance-text-to-scalar verifier with a confidence gate) OR an explicit operator ruling that ratification may be delegated/batched. That ruling has not been made.

launchFootprintCandidates.name: (a) Bastrop network only
launchFootprintCandidates.reasoning: The only candidate that is depth-satisfied TODAY at the 95 pct threshold. Bastrop city and Elgin are stamped and certified; Smithville is the one remaining city and its corpus is ingested but its stamp is honest-absent (zoning_gis null, no public FeatureServer). Launch-ready on the depth rail immediately. The cost is market size: fewer than 1 in 200 Texas parcels lands on a depth-satisfied parcel, so the statewide Smart Site claim would rest almost entirely on honest-absence. Note the operator's own governing ruling names 'the Bastrop network PLUS the initial marketed footprint', so this candidate satisfies only half the named gate.

launchFootprintCandidates.name: (b) Central Texas
launchFootprintCandidates.reasoning: Bastrop, Travis, Williamson, Hays, Caldwell, Comal, Guadalupe, Bell — the CAPCOG footprint plus the I-35 corridor to New Braunfels and Killeen. This is the footprint the repo has actually invested in: all 8 counties already carry geometry satisfied, all 8 appear in the stamp roster sweep, and 21 of the 23 stamp-capable cities in the entire state sit inside it. citiesNeeded=21 counts the cities already dry-run proven; it is a floor, not the full incorporated count. Highest ratio of market reach to remaining work. The gap is 7 counties needing stamp-apply plus warm plus cert, not 7 counties needing acquisition from scratch.

launchFootprintCandidates.name: (c) Central Texas + major metros
launchFootprintCandidates.reasoning: Adds Bexar, Dallas, Tarrant, Collin, Denton, Harris. Nearly triples parcel reach to 38.40 pct — the only candidate where a plurality of Texas users would land on a depth-satisfied parcel. But it imports the four hardest known blockers at once: Tarrant's geometry rail is still not-yet (91.58 pct) so its parcel spine is unfinished; Harris is SHORT-LOADED (the highest-priority missing instrument per OPS-12) and sharding-required; Dallas proper sits in the retired-eCode360 bucket with no proven scrape; and only San Antonio among these metros is stamp-capable today. citiesNeeded=22 counts only stamp-proven cities and is a severe undercount for six metro counties — the true number is UNKNOWN.

launchFootprintCandidates.name: (d) Statewide depth (contrast case, NOT a launch gate)
launchFootprintCandidates.reasoning: Shown for contrast only. The 2026-08-09 launch-gate ruling explicitly rejects this: making filled-everywhere the launch gate 'puts roughly 1,222 city scrapes and 254 CAD acquisitions between the product and revenue, while the product already discloses per-parcel honest absence, which is the thesis.' At the proven rate of 23 stamp-capable cities reached since the program began, and with 42 of 50 CAPCOG cities lacking any zoning_gis layer, this is the permanent post-launch engine. Compute is NOT the constraint (whole state estimated at 228.66 dollars); human ratification hours and per-city GIS probing are.

adversarialFindings: THE HEADLINE NUMBER IN THE TASK BRIEF IS WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. The brief supplied 'zoning: satisfied-present 19' as verified ground truth to rely on and not re-derive. It is literally true and materially misleading: 15 of those 19 cells carry honestCoveragePct=0 with source=null and lastVerifiedAt=null, and 3 more are partial (33.98, 25.82, 3.61). Exactly ONE county in Texas has genuine zoning depth. Had this scope accepted the supplied figure, every candidate footprint's zoningSatisfiedToday would have been inflated by up to 19x and candidate (c) would have looked 93 pct done when it is 7 pct done. The ledger's own _STATE.md says so at line 186; the live API and the state doc disagree, and the state doc is right.

THE LEDGER IS MOVING UNDER THE BRIEF. Live summary at fetch time reads totalRails 14, totalCells 3556, satisfiedCells 142, satisfiedPresentCells 160, texasCompletenessPct 4.9146 — versus _STATE.md:186's 12 rails / 3,048 cells / 19 satisfied / 0.0395 pct. Geometry moved from 19 counties to 141 satisfied. Any footprint decision must be re-read against the live ledger at decision time, not against any doc.

'SATISFIED' IS STRUCTURALLY THE WRONG PREDICATE FOR A DEPTH RAIL. For statewide-uniform rails, atomFamilyState=='present' is a fair proxy for satisfaction because the layer is acquired once and blankets the state. For depth rails it is not: one zoning atom anywhere in a county flips the whole county green. The launch-gate ruling requires depth rails to be 'satisfied in the launch-footprint counties', and the instrument that would report that satisfaction currently cannot distinguish 99.77 pct from 0 pct. RECOMMENDATION: before the footprint is ruled, the ledger must gate depth-rail satisfaction on honestCoveragePct >= thresholdPct, not on atomFamilyState. Otherwise the operator cannot read the gate they just wrote.

THE NUMBER THAT DOES NOT EXIST IS citiesNeeded. It cannot be computed for any candidate because all 1,223 city rows in texas_roster_v1.json have parent_county_fips=null. Every citiesNeeded value in this artifact is a FLOOR derived from the 23 stamp-proven cities, not a count of incorporated places in the footprint. TO SETTLE IT: spatial-join the L1 city boundary layer (txgio_city_boundaries_202508, 1,222 polygons, DONE and LIVE per _STATE.md:174) against the 254 county polygons and emit a per-county incorporated-place count. That join is cheap, read-only, and needs no acquisition — the data is already loaded. It is the single highest-value missing number for this decision, and it also repairs the T6 roster's failed acceptance criterion.

THE SECOND MISSING NUMBER IS ZONED-CITY SHARE. Even a correct city count overstates the work: Texas counties cannot zone by law, and 61a_central_tx_coverage_program.md:71 records that over half of the corridor's ~120 incorporated places are sub-2,000-population no-zoning towns correctly treated as demand-driven Tier-B. The CAPCOG registry bears this out: of 50 cities, 46 have_zoning true, 3 unzoned, 2 unknown, and regime_type splits euclidean 38 / hybrid 6 / unzoned 3 / form-based 1 / unknown 2. So the real denominator for candidate (b) is closer to the Tier-A deal-volume cities than to the raw incorporated count. Until the boundary join runs, treat citiesNeeded as UNKNOWN with a known floor.

PARCEL SHARE IS THE ONLY DECISION INPUT THAT IS SOLID, AND IT FAVORS (b). Using parcel_count_est across 254/254 counties (13,360,496 total; only 48129 Hemphill null): (a) 0.47 pct, (b) 12.66 pct, (c) 38.40 pct. The jump from (a) to (b) buys 27x the market reach for 7 counties that already have satisfied geometry and 21 already-dry-run-proven city stamps. The jump from (b) to (c) buys 3x more reach but imports Tarrant's unfinished geometry, Harris's undetectable short-load, Dallas's unproven scrape path, and six metro counties with essentially no stamp-capable cities. On evidence, (b) is the efficient frontier — but this is a data-readiness argument, not a demand argument, and demand is the operator's input.

THE HUMANLESS RULING AND THE Z5 GATE CANNOT BOTH STAND. Z5 (operator ratification of the setback table) is not an automation gap that engineering can close incidentally — it exists precisely because no instrument grades a per-parcel setback record against ordinance text, and OPS-12 lists that as a defect class with no instrument. The operator must make ONE of three rulings before any multi-city footprint is committed: (i) build the ordinance-text-to-scalar verifier with a confidence gate and let it ratify below a threshold; (ii) delegate or batch ratification explicitly, accepting the risk; or (iii) accept ~1 human-hour per city and size the footprint to the hours available. NAMED RULING NOT YET MADE. Candidate (b) is 21+ hours under (iii); candidate (d) is 1,223.

COST IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT AND SHOULD STOP BEING DISCUSSED AS ONE. The full 254-county state is estimated at 228.66 dollars of compute — less than the per-jurisdiction budget for a SINGLE county. The most expensive county in Texas is Travis at 14.29. The Bastrop 284.40 outlier is a low-confidence after-the-fact reconstruction across six warm passes that the operator already ruled do not count. The binding constraints on L5 are human ratification hours and per-city GIS probing, in that order. Commitment #3's compute half is comfortably met; its 1-hour-human-review half has never been measured at all, and OPS-11 marks the invariant UNENFORCED.

RELEASING THE STAMP HOLD IS THE CHEAPEST MOVE ON THE BOARD. 23 cities totalling roughly 1.09M parcels are already dry-run proven with exitCode 0 and zero errors across 10 counties, blocked only by a blast-radius review pending ldt #386. Applying those stamps would move Bell, Bexar, Caldwell, Guadalupe, McLennan and Travis off zero coverage and would convert most of candidate (b) from paper to measured — at close to zero acquisition cost, since the probing and the dry-runs are already paid for. This should be sequenced before any new city acquisition.

DO NOT TRUST 'wired' AS A SYNONYM FOR 'stamped', AND DO NOT TRUST THE REGISTRY AS THE LIST OF WIRED CITIES. The stamp roster is dry-run-only, and the registry's zoning_gis field is stale in both directions: Elgin shows null yet was successfully stamped via a FeatureServer discovered during Z1 recon, while 8 rows carry endpoints marked trust='untested' (7 of 8) or 'drift-detected' (Bastrop). The authoritative statement of which cities can be stamped is a fresh dry-run, not either artifact.
